themes_detail.label: Garbage Collection Breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Missed collection complaints spiked to 36 this week vs. 5.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (513% increase, z-score 4.55), suggesting a significant sanitation system failure hitting Williamsbridge/Baychester residents in the past 7 days.
evidence: 36 missed collection complaints last week vs. 5.9 weekly average (513% spike)
Z-score of 4.55 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Spike is THIS WEEK, not historical — represents acute service breakdown
reporting_angles: Interview residents with uncollected trash piling up; determine if weather, staffing shortages, or route changes caused failure
Contact NYC Sanitation to determine scope: Is this district-wide or localized to specific neighborhoods? Are collections being rerouted?

themes_detail.label: Electrical Hazards Surge
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints jumped to 4 last week vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (700% increase, z-score 7.0), indicating a potential wave of electrical system failures or safety hazards across the district over the past 7 days.
evidence: 4 electrical complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (700% increase)
Z-score of 7.0 indicates very high statistical significance
Timing: last week — emerging issue requiring immediate investigation
reporting_angles: Map the 4 electrical complaints geographically — are they clustered or scattered? Could indicate infrastructure failure vs. isolated incidents.
Interview Con Edison about service issues; ask if aging grid infrastructure in Williamsbridge/Baychester is a known concern or if recent weather has stressed the system.

themes_detail.label: Dead and Dying Trees Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints exploded to 3 two weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% spike, z-score 8.69), marking the most statistically extreme anomaly in the dataset and suggesting either major environmental stress, disease outbreak, or tree maintenance collapse in the district.
evidence: 3 dead/dying tree complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% increase)
Z-score of 8.69 — highest statistical severity in entire dataset
Repeated CB budget request for 'new equipment for maintenance' (Parks Dept) signals chronic underfunding of tree care
reporting_angles: Visit the specific locations of the 3 complaints; assess whether this is storm damage, disease (emerald ash borer, other pests), or neglect
Interview Parks Department about tree inventory and maintenance schedule in CD212; connect spike to underfunded equipment request in CB budget.

themes_detail.label: Hazardous Materials & Animal Incidents
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 2 weeks, hazardous materials complaints (3, up 1100% from 0.2 baseline, z-score 6.35) and unleashed dog incidents (3, up 1100%, z-score 6.35) both spiked simultaneously, raising questions about whether environmental contamination and loose animals are linked to a single source (construction, illegal dumping, or park mismanagement).
evidence: Hazardous materials: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% increase, z-score 6.35)
Unleashed dogs: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% increase, z-score 6.35)
Convergence of identical spike timing and magnitude suggests possible common cause (e.g., park closure, cleanup operation, construction site)
reporting_angles: Cross-reference the 3 hazmat and 3 unleashed dog complaints by location — are they in the same park or neighborhood block? Convergence could indicate a single incident (illegal dumping, contaminated site).
Interview NYC Department of Health and Parks Dept about whether they are coordinating response to environmental contamination that may be displacing animals.

themes_detail.label: Sanitation System Strain
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 2-3 weeks, residential disposal complaints (9, up 200% from 3 baseline, z-score 4.54 two weeks ago) and street sweeping complaints (10, up 700% from 1.2 baseline, z-score 4.28 three weeks ago) both surged, suggesting broader sanitation infrastructure stress beyond the acute missed collection crisis.
evidence: Street sweeping complaints: 10 (3 weeks ago) vs. 1.2 weekly average (700% increase, z-score 4.28)
Residential disposal complaints: 9 (2 weeks ago) vs. 3.0 weekly average (200% increase, z-score 4.54)
Pattern spans 2-3 weeks, overlaps with this week's garbage collection crisis, indicates systemic sanitation problems
reporting_angles: Ask NYC Sanitation if staffing shortages, budget cuts, or equipment failures are cascading across collection, street sweeping, and disposal services.
Document visual conditions on streets: accumulating trash, debris, and lack of sweeping — provide photo evidence of sanitation system breakdown.
